_what: Per-type state decisions that cannot be derived from the tree, read by tools/gen-atlas.py.
_why: atlas/catalog-data.json's `state` is generated, not hand-written, for the same reason `built` is: a fact kept honest only by memory drifts, and this one is public. `built` is derived from the bundles on disk. `out-of-scope` and `queued` cannot be, because they are decisions rather than facts about the tree, so they live here where each carries a reason and an ADR. Everything not named here defaults to `candidate`.
_vocabulary: built (derived) | queued (a build the maintainer intends) | candidate (eligible, unranked, the default) | out-of-scope (refused, on a stated ground). Set by ADR 0041, which replaced `pull-gated` because that name asserted a gate ADR 0039 had already removed.
_rule: Keep this file small. Every entry carries a reason naming an ADR or an issue. A type listed here that also has a bundle on disk is a contradiction and gen-atlas.py fails on it.

out-of-scope.wireframe: Not a document. ADR 0030 declared catalog 52 out of scope: no named source publishes a 'wireframe specification' as a written document, so shipping one would invent a document type nobody writes to fill a catalog slot.
out-of-scope.interactive-prototype: Not a document. ADR 0030 declared catalog 54 out of scope on the same admission test: flows, interactions, states and transitions are not a written artifact a Markdown template can produce.

queued.epic: A build the maintainer set on 2026-09-01 under ADR 0041, whose rationale is recorded as: closes the requirements spine between product-roadmap and user-stories, and is the type most likely to arrive in WP-33 wedge outreach. Family membership admitted by ADR 0042, which amended contracts/delivery-docs.md to 0.1.3.
